<section class="section wrap intro-grid">
<div>
<p class="eyebrow">Research perspective</p>
<h2>What can geophysical observations tell us about the subsurface?</h2>
</div>
<div>
<p>I am a Ph.D. candidate in Geophysics at Stony Brook University, working with Weisen Shen. My research seeks to understand what geophysical observations can tell us about the subsurface, from its structure to its composition, temperature, porosity, and fluid conditions.</p>
<p>During my Ph.D., I have approached these questions primarily through seismology. I develop and apply joint-inversion methods that combine complementary seismic observations to improve constraints on crustal structure and reduce trade-offs between model parameters.</p>
<p>My current research extends these questions to polar environments. In Antarctica, I use seismic observations together with radar and magnetotelluric constraints to investigate the elastic properties and hydrological conditions of the subglacial environment. Polar environments will be a central focus of my future research.</p>
</div>
</section>
